domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The speaker leads product engineering for Google's Jules coding agent and frames the entire event around AI coding as the most important problem in applied AI. Jules is a coding assistant product and the summit targets software builders across the AI coding industry. Jules and Gemini 3 are described as released products in active use. This is a welcoming opening keynote with no technical prerequisites or depth. The video is a conference opening address by the Day 2 MC. All key claims are directly stated in the transcript by the speaker.

summary: Jed Borovik opens Day 2 of the 2025 AI Engineering Code Summit in New York on a Friday morning, welcoming returning and first-time attendees. He introduces himself as Gemini's assistant at Google and leader of the product engineering team for the Jules coding agent, and notes he is the day's MC. He anchors the event's purpose in Richard Hamming's famous talk, recalling Hamming's habit of asking colleagues what the most important problem in their field is, then asking why they are not working on it. Jed applies this lens to the audience: AI is the most important problem in technology, and for applied AI, code is the most important problem. He emphasizes that the summit is designed to push the entire AI coding industry forward, not to serve any single company. The AI Engineering Conference has two brands: a world's fair and a summit; this is the smaller, single-track summit, intentionally bringing together top people around the single theme of AI coding. He references yesterday's leadership track, which focused on how AI is transforming software organizations, and says today will dive into the patterns, systems, and products that enable those transformations. Audience members shout out favorite leadership-track talks, including ones from Stanford, Jean and Steve, and Dan. Jed thanks sponsors, especially presenting sponsor DeepMind, platinum sponsor Anthropic, and various gold and silver sponsors, encouraging attendees to visit sponsor booths in the expo area after keynotes. He highlights the week's product launches, Gemini 3 and Nano Banana Pro, before transitioning to the first session.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Opening Welcome and Audience Interaction
sections.summary: Jed Borovik opens Day 2 of the 2025 AI Engineering Code Summit in New York on a Friday morning, with music and applause. He gauges prior conference attendance by show of hands, finding about half the audience had attended before, with a small number having attended multiple prior events. He jokes with an audience member, Alex, about the count of past events.

sections.title: Self-Introduction and Hamming Framing
sections.summary: Jed introduces himself as Gemini's assistant at Google and leader of the product engineering team for the Jules coding agent, and the day's MC. He invokes Richard Hamming's famous talk, where Hamming asked colleagues about the most important problem in their field and why they were not working on it. Jed applies this to the audience: AI is the most important problem in technology, and code is the most important problem in applied AI.

sections.title: Event Purpose and Summit Format
sections.summary: Jed explains the summit is meant to push the entire AI coding industry forward, not to serve a single company. The AI Engineering Conference has two brands: a world's fair and a summit. This summit is intentionally smaller and single-track, designed to bring the best people together around the single important theme of AI coding.

sections.title: Leadership Track Recap and Audience Shoutouts
sections.summary: Jed references yesterday's leadership track about how AI is transforming software organizations, and asks attendees to shout out favorite talks. Audience members mention talks from Stanford, Jean and Steve, and Dan. Jed previews today's focus on the patterns, systems, and products that make those organizational transformations possible.

sections.title: Sponsor Acknowledgments and Product Launches
sections.summary: Jed thanks sponsors, especially presenting sponsor DeepMind, platinum sponsor Anthropic, and gold and silver sponsors shown on screen. He highlights the week's releases of Gemini 3 and Nano Banana Pro, encourages attendees to visit sponsor booths in the expo area after keynotes, and transitions to the first session with music.
